answers.explanation: A name you own can't be registered by someone else, and won't clash with a TLD that's created later.
If the office loses power and your only nameserver is there, mail can't even find your backup MX.
Internal names belong in the internal view. Staff at home reach them over the VPN.
Dynamic DNS keeps names pointing at the right addresses as laptops come and go.
An open resolver is an amplification weapon. Serve your own users only.
Otherwise one AXFR hands anyone a map of your network.
Users keep the service name; only the alias's target changes.
A primary and a secondary, in different places, so one failure doesn't take every name down.
If laptops use some public resolver instead, they can't see internal names, and you can't see suspicious lookups.
